append.text: **Ps 14:1 *Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo?* → *Senhor, quem habitará na vossa tenda?*** — God's tent, as this row foresaw; passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'living with the Lord' first and the concrete tent second. *no vosso tabernáculo* (MS1932) is the option. 31 lines (grep), God's and men's alike (77:51 *in tabernáculis Cham*, 83:11 *tabernáculis peccatórum*), which *tabernáculo* (a church's, in Brazil) could not serve.

**Ps 14:3a *qui non egit dolum in lingua sua* → *que não usou de engano com a sua língua*** (the noun kept; the light verb *usar de*, DRB's 'used deceit'; *com* for the instrumental in, from the stylist). Not the one verb *enganar* of 5:11a / 13:3b, because 14:4b has *décipere* (→ *não engana*; Greek ἀθετῶν) — a noun and a verb of one family for two Latin words. The stylist's *praticou engano* refused: *praticar* is operári's (14:2). **23:4 *nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo* (this psalm's cousin) → *nem jurou com engano ao seu próximo*.**
Ps 14:4a *Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus* → *À vista dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada* — D24 applied (one of the singular places this row named); no reader remarked.

**Ps 14:4a *in conspéctu ejus* → *À vista dele*:** the stylist asked for *Aos olhos dele* ('à vista' sounded like physical presence) — refused, *olho* is óculus's; the blind reader heard 'aos olhos do homem descrito', the judging look, rightly. Evidence for *vista* again (9:20, 9:26a, 14:4a).
Ps 14:4a *timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat* → *mas glorifica os que temem o Senhor* — a man glorifying men; *honra* (MS1932, DM1962) is the option; passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 14:5b *non movébitur in ætérnum* → *para sempre não será abalado*:** D23's words, the adverb before the negation as 118:93, so that 'never' is the only hearing (the blind reader: 'Permanecerá firme'). **The stylist's worst line** ('soa estrangeira'); he wants *jamais será abalado* (the Diurnal's), which drops in ætérnum's word — option in Ps 14. 124:1 *non commovébitur in ætérnum* and 111:6 *in ætérnum non commovébitur* will meet the same choice; commovéri (15:8 *ne commóvear*, 13 lines) shares the verb, one Greek (σαλεύω).

**Ps 14:5b — D23 under a negation:** *para sempre não será abalado* (the 118:93 build). The Latinist passed it twice and the blind reader heard 'never'; the stylist refused it as foreign and asked for *jamais* — for Gustavo's ear: this is where D23 costs most.

Ps 14:3b *Nec fecit próximo suo malum* → *nem fez ao seu próximo o mal* (the Latin's order, so that the mediant falls on *mal*; the stylist's *fez mal ao seu próximo* is the option, refused under rule 4) and *e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta* (the phrase fronted so that the verse does not end on *próximos*). 14:4b *jura ao seu próximo* (not at a cadence).

Ps 14:3b *oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos* → *não aceitou afronta contra os seus próximos*: heard by the blind reader as 'did not tolerate offences against his neighbours' first and 'did not take up an accusation against them' second (the Latin's letter); passed the Latinist twice.

terms: | ingrédi (walking) | andar (*Aquele que anda sem mancha*) | open | Ps 14:2 *Qui ingréditur sine mácula* — L&S 'to go into, enter' and 'to go, walk'; the Greek πορευόμενος fixes 'walk', the verb the glossary renders *andar* for ambuláre and abíre (1:1). 25:1, 25:11 *ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum* (grep) can follow (*andei na minha inocência*). *entrar* stays for íngredi into a place (117:19 the gates). Passed the Latinist twice and the blind reader. Options *caminha* (DM1962), *entra* |
| sine mácula | sem mancha | working | Ps 14:2 only (grep); immaculátus keeps *imaculado* (118:1, 118:80) |

| décipere | enganar (*e não engana*) | open | Ps 14:4b (Greek ἀθετῶν); 61:10 *ut decípiant*, 76:3 *non sum decéptus* (grep: 3 lines). Takes the verb *enganar*, so dolus in the same psalm keeps the noun *engano* (14:3a *não usou de engano*). No object supplied (MS1932 *não o engana* is the option) |

| usúra | usura (*que não deu o seu dinheiro à usura*) | open | Ps 14:4b; 54:12 *usúra, et dolus*, 71:14 *Ex usúris et iniquitáte* (grep). The cognate keeps the reproach those two verses need; listed as unknown by the blind reader. Option *a juros* |

| múnera | dádivas | open | Ps 14:4b *nem aceitou dádivas contra o inocente* (heard as a bribe without the word); must serve the kings' gifts 67:30, 71:10, 75:12 (grep), so not *subornos* (DRB). Option *presentes* |

| dedúcere / redígere ad níhilum | reduzir a nada (*o malvado foi reduzido a nada*) | open | Ps 14:4a (ἐξουδένωται). The same phrase 58:9, 59:14 = 107:14 (*ad níhilum dedúcet* → *reduzirá a nada*), with redígere 72:20, 77:59, 72:21 *ad níhilum redáctus sum* (grep; the Greek of those not checked). *reduzir* is re-dúcere. Heard by the blind reader as 'destroyed before him' first, 'esteemed worthless' second — both in the Latin |
| requiéscere | repousar | working | Ps 4:9 *repousarei*, 14:1 *quem repousará no vosso monte santo?*, 15:9 *repousará na esperança*, 54:7 (grep: 4 lines) |
| mons sanctus | monte santo (adjective after) | working | Ps 2:6, 14:1 (*no vosso monte santo*); 3:5, 42:3, 47:2, 98:9 (grep) |

| *Qui … qui …* answering *quis?* (Ps 14) | *Aquele que … que …* | open | Ps 14:2, 3a, 4b, 5b — one decision, six slots; *O que* (MS1932) at the head of a verse can be heard as 'what'. Ps 23:4 (*Ínnocens mánibus … qui non accépit*) is the cousin psalm and may follow |
formulas: | *Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum* (14:5b; 124:1 *non commovébitur in ætérnum*, 111:6 *in ætérnum non commovébitur*) | *… para sempre não será abalado* | open — Ps 14; the stylist's worst line, *jamais será abalado* the option (D23's cost) |
